Kuvitus: olohuoneen katossa on valkoinen: Illustration: a white round smoke detector on the ceiling of a living room, partly drawn cut open. Inside, in a chamber between two metal plates, is a small americium sample, from which short violet particle tracks go out into the air. The room has a window and a ceiling lamp.
Kaksi hiilen ydintä vierekkäin, ei mitta: Two carbon nuclei side by side, not to scale. On the left carbon-12: six red protons and six grey neutrons, written with 12 as a superscript and 6 as a subscript in front of C. On the right carbon-14: six protons and eight neutrons. Both have six protons, so they are isotopes of the same element. At the bottom the key: a red ball is a proton, a grey one a neutron.
Nuklidikartta kaavamaisesti: vaaka-aksel: Chart of nuclides, schematic: the neutron number N from zero to 140 on the horizontal axis and the atomic number Z from zero to 90 on the vertical axis. The green band is the region of stable nuclei. For light nuclei it runs close to the dashed line N = Z, for heavy ones it bends below it, because stable heavy nuclei have more neutrons than protons. Below the band there are too many neutrons and the nucleus decays by beta minus decay, above it there are too few neutrons and the nucleus decays by beta plus decay. At the upper end of the band, Z above 82, heavy nuclei often decay by alpha decay: the violet arrow to the right of the upper end of the band points diagonally down and to the left, because alpha decay reduces both the neutron number and the atomic number by two.
Kolme hajoamislajia vierekkäin, kaavakuv: Three kinds of decay side by side, a schematic figure, not to scale. On the left alpha decay: an alpha particle, a helium nucleus made of two protons and two neutrons, leaves the nucleus, and the atomic number of the nucleus decreases by two and the mass number by four. In the middle beta minus decay: a neutron of the nucleus changes into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino leave the nucleus, the atomic number increases by one and the mass number stays the same. On the right gamma decay: a nucleus in an excited state emits a gamma photon, and the atomic number and the mass number stay the same.
Energiatasokaavio, energiat mittakaavass: Energy level diagram, energies to scale: cobalt-60 decays by beta minus decay to an excited state of nickel-60 whose energy is 2505.8 keV above the ground state. The nucleus returns to the ground state in two steps: first to the level 1332.5 keV, emitting a gamma photon of 1173.2 keV, and then to the ground state, emitting a gamma photon of 1332.5 keV. Data from the NNDC NuDat database.
Nuklidikartan ote, ruudukko: vaaka-aksel: Part of a chart of nuclides, a grid: the neutron number N on the horizontal axis and the atomic number Z on the vertical axis, one cell is one unit. In the middle is the parent nucleus. Alpha decay moves the nucleus two cells down and two to the left (Z − 2, N − 2). Beta minus decay moves it one cell up and one to the left (Z + 1, N − 1). Beta plus decay moves it one cell down and one to the right (Z − 1, N + 1). In gamma decay the nucleus stays in the same cell.
